translations.source_sense_description: Avec un adjectif ou un adverbe, signifie son comparatif

glosses: A person or thing that does an action indicated by the root verb; used to form an agent noun.

run + -er → runner
toast + -er → toaster

glosses: A person or thing to which the root verb is done or can be done satisfactorily.

examples.text: look + -er → looker (“an attractive person”)
keep + -er → keeper (“a person or thing worth keeping”)

glosses: A person whose occupation is the root noun; (more broadly, occasionally with adjectives) a person characterized by the root.

examples.text: astrology + -er → astrologer
baby boom + -er → baby boomer
conlang + -er → conlanger
cricket + -er → cricketer
trumpet + -er → trumpeter
zine + -er → ziner

glosses: A person or thing to which a certain number or measurement applies.

examples.text: six + -er → sixer
six foot + -er → six-footer
three-wheel + -er → three-wheeler

glosses: Used to form nouns shorter than more formal synonyms.

examples.text: percent + -er → percenter (“commission agent”)
one hand + -er → one-hander (“one-man show”)
oat + -er → oater (“a Western-themed movie”)

glosses: A person who is associated with, or supports a particular theory, doctrine, or political movement.

examples.text: birth + -er → birther
flat earth + -er → flat-earther
truth + -er → truther
woke + -er → woker

glosses: A thing that is related in some way to the root, such as by location or purpose.

examples.text: bacon + -er → baconer (“pig raised for bacon”)
chocolate chip + -er → chocolate chipper (“cookie containing chocolate chips”)
sternwheel + -er → sternwheeler (“vessel driven by a sternwheel”)

glosses: Indicates a correspondence or coincidence between the action or condition indicated by the root and the noun being described.

examples.text: piss + -er → pisser (“a hilariously funny event or situation”)

glosses: Suffix denoting a resident or inhabitant of (the place denoted by the proper noun); used to form a demonym.

examples.text: New York + -er → New Yorker
London + -er → Londoner
Dublin + -er → Dubliner
New England + -er → New Englander

glosses: Suffix denoting residency in or around a place, district, area, or region.

examples.text: island + -er → islander
highland + -er → highlander
East End + -er → East-Ender

glosses: Suffix used to form the plural of a small number of English nouns.

examples.text: childer, calver, lamber, linder ("loins")

glosses: More; used to form the comparative.

examples.text: eerie + -er → eerier
clayey + -er → clayier
hard + -er → harder
wet + -er → wetter
motley + -er → motlier

glosses: More; used to form the comparative.
Frequently; used to form frequentative verbs.

examples.text: twitter, clamber, bicker, mutter, wander, flutter, flicker, slither, smother, sputter

glosses: Instance of (the verbal action); used to form nouns from verbs.

examples.text: disclaim + -er → disclaimer
remit + -er → remitter
misname + -er → misnomer
rebut + -er → rebutter
attain + -er → attainder

glosses: Used to form diminutives.

examples.text: shive + -er → shiver
slive + -er → sliver
splint + -er → splinter

glosses: Used to form slang or colloquial equivalents of words.

examples.text: association + -er → soccer (“association football”)
football + -er → footer (“association football”)
rugby + -er → rugger
Radcliffe + -er → Radder (“a building at Oxford University”)

glosses: A suffix creating adjectives from verbs, indicating aptitude, proneness, or tendency toward a specified action

examples.text: clive + -er → cliver (“apt to cleave or adhere to, tenacious, expert as seizing”)
slip + -er → slipper (“tending to make slip, slippery”)
wake + -er → waker (“tending to wake, watchful”)

glosses: Junior, child, younger person. (Attached to a name, usually one syllable of the given name.)

examples.text: Li’er said hello to his father.
Yue’er began to laugh again and her tears shimmered like dew on a lotus leaf disturbed by a breeze. Then we heard a sound. It was Man’er.

glosses: comparative degree of many: in greater number. (Used for a discrete quantity.)

examples.text: 宋·司馬光《乞罷保甲札子》：“若見充弓手人有勇力武藝衰退，許他人指名比較，若勝於舊者，即令充替。”

examples.text: 宋·司馬光《二十六日作真率會別用韻》：“座中七叟推年紀，比較前人少幾多。”
毛澤東《＜農村調查＞的序言和跋》：“開調查會……這是比較什麼大學還要高明的學校。”

glosses: 表示具有一定程度。

examples.text: 毛澤東《論人民民主專政》：“錯誤和挫折教訓了我們，使我們比較地聰明起來了。”
